summary: Follow-up to iteration_9/10 testing the new COOP/COEP (crossOriginIsolated) headers added to craco.config.js dev server, to check if they fix the vendor Tint/Banuba VTO widget's silent infinite hang. CONFIRMED: window.crossOriginIsolated === true and typeof SharedArrayBuffer !== 'undefined' === true on https://kinetic-medtech-ui.preview.emergentagent.com/xofit-frame-fitting - the headers ARE achieving real cross-origin isolation in the browser, not just present in raw HTTP headers (verified both via curl and page.evaluate). HOWEVER, the underlying widget behavior is IDENTICAL to iteration_9/10: after clicking [data-testid='vto-trigger-button'], the widget's branded overlay opens (~1s) and then hangs on its internal spinner forever with ZERO console output at any level (info/log/warn/error - only 1 unrelated React DevTools info log across the whole session) and ZERO network errors (all ~30 vendor requests including BanubaSDK.simd-d6b22068.wasm returned 200, loaded 3 times due to repeated init attempts). No camera permission prompt appeared, no product grid rendered, no progress past the spinner was observed at any of the 10 sampling checkpoints (t=3s to t=30s). Our app's 20s stuck-timer toast correctly fired at t=21s and auto-dismissed by t=27s (consistent with iteration_10's known auto-dismiss timing), confirming our fallback UX still works correctly but the vendor widget itself never became ready. This DISPROVES the SharedArrayBuffer/cross-origin-isolation theory as the root cause - isolation is now real and available, yet the hang is byte-for-byte the same silent black-box hang as before. Regression: tab switching (core/mobile/frame/core) on Fit page and Home page load cleanly with 0 new console errors and 0 broken images with the new headers active; only the same pre-existing unrelated 'fetchpriority' React DOM prop-casing warning on Home page (also seen in iteration_9) was present.

ui_bugs.issue: Even with window.crossOriginIsolated=true and SharedArrayBuffer available (new COOP/COEP headers confirmed active and effective), the widget still opens its branded overlay then hangs forever on its internal spinner with zero console output and zero network errors - identical behavior to iteration_9/10 before the headers were added. This disproves the SharedArrayBuffer-requirement theory as the root cause of the hang.

action_items: The crossOriginIsolated/SharedArrayBuffer headers fix does NOT resolve the widget hang. window.crossOriginIsolated=true and SharedArrayBuffer available were both confirmed true in a real browser, yet the vendor widget hangs identically to before. This is now a confirmed pure vendor black-box issue, not a SharedArrayBuffer/WASM-SIMD isolation problem.

Recommend escalating directly to the Tint/Banuba vendor with the confirmed facts: all assets load 200 (including BanubaSDK.simd wasm), crossOriginIsolated is true, SharedArrayBuffer is available, zero console/network errors, yet SDK never fires any ready/error event or produces any console output after the overlay opens. Ask vendor specifically what event/condition their SDK expects post-WASM-load that might be silently failing (e.g. a different feature-detection check, a WebGL context requirement, or a merchant config issue specific to this account's config.json/UUID).
The COOP/COEP headers are safe to keep - regression testing found no new broken images or console errors on Fit page tab switching or Home/System pages from adding these headers.
No production Netlify verification possible yet per problem statement (headers only in netlify.toml, not yet deployed) - retest on production once deployed.
critical_code_review_comments: craco.config.js's makeDevServerV5Compatible() correctly injects Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy/Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy/Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy headers into the dev server response - verified effective via both curl (raw headers present) and page.evaluate (window.crossOriginIsolated=true, SharedArrayBuffer available), so the implementation of this specific change is correct and working as intended.

Fit.jsx's 20s stuck-timer toast (from iteration_10) continues to work correctly as a UX safety net and fired reliably again at ~21s in this run - this remains the only currently-effective mitigation for the vendor hang.

success_rate.frontend: 100% for the specific tests requested - COOP/COEP header effectiveness confirmed, regression clean; but the underlying vendor VTO widget issue itself remains unresolved (0% fix rate for the actual reported bug)

context_for_next_testing_agent: This closes out the SharedArrayBuffer/crossOriginIsolated theory started in this iteration's problem statement. CONFIRMED FACTS: (1) window.crossOriginIsolated=true and SharedArrayBuffer available on the preview URL with the new headers (both curl and JS-runtime verified), (2) the tint-vto widget hang is byte-for-byte identical before and after this change - same overlay-opens-then-silent-spinner-forever behavior, same zero console output, same all-200 network (BanubaSDK.simd-d6b22068.wasm loads fine, 3x due to repeated init attempts across the 30s window), (3) our 20s stuck-timer toast fired correctly at t=21s confirming Fit.jsx's fallback logic is unaffected and still working. CONCLUSION for main agent: the SharedArrayBuffer theory was disproven - this is a pure vendor SDK black-box issue unrelated to cross-origin isolation. Next steps should be vendor escalation (contact Tint/Banuba support with the specific merchant UUID f3339032-dafa-47fe-bb1e-79a965fd4118 and note that isolation headers are confirmed active yet SDK still never emits any lifecycle event), not further header/config tweaking on our side. Headless Chromium camera limitation was NOT the blocker either since no camera-permission prompt was ever reached - the hang happens before that stage, likely during BanubaSDK WASM module instantiation/execution itself (loads via network fine, but something after that silently fails with no error surfaced to console).
rca_of_the_issue: Disproven theory: the client developer's SharedArrayBuffer/cross-origin-isolation hypothesis (WASM SIMD build requiring COOP+COEP headers) was directly tested and ruled out - isolation is confirmed real and active (window.crossOriginIsolated=true, SharedArrayBuffer available) yet the hang persists identically. The true root cause remains unidentified and is inside the vendor's closed-source WASM/JS bundle (tintvto.com/xenonophthalmics/assets/*), which produces zero observable console/network signal of any failure - this is not diagnosable further from the client side without vendor SDK debug logging or vendor support access to their build/error-reporting pipeline.
